title: Count Complete Tree Nodes
summary: Given the root of a complete binary tree, calculate the total number of nodes in the tree with a time complexity better than O(n).
statement: Given the root of a complete binary tree, calculate the total number of nodes in the tree with a time complexity better than O(n). A complete binary tree has all levels fully filled except possibly the last, where nodes are as far left as possible.
constraints: 0–50000 tree nodes with integer values from 0 to 50000. The tree is guaranteed complete: all levels except possibly the last are full, and the last is filled from left to right.
Return the number of nodes, regardless of repeated values. Use the complete-tree structure to achieve sublinear time rather than visiting every node.

hints: Completeness guarantees that one of the current root's subtrees is perfect.
Compare the left-edge heights of the left and right children to identify the perfect subtree.
If heights match, add 2^left_height for the root plus its perfect left subtree and continue right; otherwise add 2^right_height and continue left.
A perfect subtree of height h has 2^h-1 nodes; including the current root makes the skipped contribution 2^h.
editorial: At each complete subtree, equal child left-edge heights mean the left child is perfect; otherwise the right child is perfect one level shorter. Count that perfect side in constant arithmetic and descend only into the remaining side. There are logarithmically many descents and each pair of height scans is logarithmic, giving O(log²(n+1)) time and constant extra space. The independent oracle simply counts the complete level-order input entries. Regression tests additionally count node-link reads, distinguishing the advertised sublinear reference from a full traversal; ordinary submissions still receive behavioral correctness and a time deadline, not a symbolic complexity proof.
